_baseline_note: E007: BERT-small T cell, f0, seed 0, eval every 1500 iters. Test: ACC 65.28 / AUC 67.88 / llm AP 88.58; best_val 66.36 at iter 1500, val AUC decayed at 3000 and 4500. Same early-peak pattern in E006 (BERT-mini). BERT-base T_base: 91.60.

factor._note: Validation (and best-checkpoint selection by val AUC) every 500 iters instead of 1500. Training schedule, LR, iters, patience count (8 evals) unchanged; patience window shrinks from 12000 to 4000 iters, which cannot cut a run whose peak is at or before 1500 any differently than before.

hypothesis: The small BERTs peak before or between the coarse 1500-iter validation points, so a 3x finer validation grid selects a better checkpoint and recovers part of the 3.02-point gap to BERT-base: f0 test llm AP > 88.58, target >= 91.0; if the curve is flat between 1000 and 2000 the gain is ~0 and the gap is capacity/LR, not selection granularity.
_success_note: test.mAP == llm_textgen AP (nkeep=1). Verdict is strict-sign vs E007 (88.58); the user's target is 91.60 (BERT-base). If <= 88.58: eval granularity is not the lever -> try peak_lr 2e-5 on this cell, or BERT-medium (41M).

watched.best_val_iter: where the val AUC peak lands on the 500 grid (E007: 1500 on the 1500 grid)
